## Science beyond the lab

<p style="font-size:14px; color:#4B5563; max-width:860px; line-height:1.75; margin-bottom:36px;">
We believe research should speak to more than specialists. Here are some of the ways we have tried to bring microbial evolution to broader audiences.
</p>

```{=html}

  <p class="outreach-desc">We collaborated with a comic book artist, <a href="https://pawelpiechnik.com/pl" target="_blank">Paweł Piechnik</a>, to create an illustrated story about bacteriophages and why they are important for the society. The comic is aimed at everyone and no biology background is required. We hope you like it! Available in Polish and English.</p>

<div class="outreach-entry">

  <span class="outreach-pill pill-lecture">Lecture</span>
</div>
<div>
  <p class="outreach-title">Public lecture: How evolutionary biology helps us fight pathogens</p>
  <p class="outreach-desc">Darwin Day public lecture at Adam Mickiewicz University, Poznań. The talk introduced evolutionary arms races between bacteria and their viruses, and how computational genomics is helping to understand — and eventually exploit — these dynamics.</p>
```
